newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour's Blair says no plan to end union link.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour's Blair says no plan to end union link.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party leader Tony Blair said he had no plans to end the institutional link with Britain's trade unions. "There are no proposals to end the institutional link," he told BBC radio. "But the relationship has already evolved enormously. This year at party conference for the first time, constituency delegates will have a majority of the vote."
He said trade unions can make their demands on the Labour Party as other people can. "But in the end, we govern for Britain."

Blair said there were four key challenges for the next government to face -- to compete in the global market place, to reform the welfare state, to decentralise the political system to give more power at the grass roots and to regain influence abroad.
Blair said those were the issues he will address in a speech to business leaders he will deliver later on Monday, in London.
He is due to give the LIFFE city lecture in London's Guildhall, starting at around 1645 GMT.
Blair said any minimum wage had to be set at a realistic level but noted that the United States and most of Europe had minimum wage legislation.
"I don't believe...that you can compete on a low wage, low skill basis," he said.
